explanation: REQ-6-1 states that any valid Request changes blocks merging and that a blocked PR keeps only a non-actionable merge control. The fixture uses the seeded Open PR acme-docs#1 (base main, current compare commit c-acme-3) whose branch protection enables both rules; the required `test` check is set to success and a valid non-author approval from bob-reviewer exists, while dana-dev — added with the minimal Write grant needed for the scenario — has a non-stale 'Changes requested' review on the current compare commit. The handler that renders the merge area (APP.pullSidebar) derives eligibility from the approval count alone, so it renders an enabled Merge pull request control although a valid Request changes review blocks the merge.
subject: pullSidebar

explanation: REQ-6-5 requires that when the target branch is protected each enabled rule is enforced independently, so an Open PR with a valid non-author approval but a `test` check that is not success must stay blocked (non-actionable Merge pull request control plus the unmet-condition explanation). The seeded PR acme-docs#1 targets protected main with both Require 1 approval and Require status check test enabled; bob-reviewer's approval is valid and non-stale for the current compare commit c-acme-3, while the seeded check record for that same commit is still 'pending'. APP.pullSidebar never reads the check rule when computing merge eligibility, so it renders an enabled Merge pull request control for a PR that the protection rule requires to be blocked.

explanation: REQ-5-3-1 defines assignable members as accounts holding at least Triage permission on the current repository and states that non-assignable users do not appear in the results. In the seed, carol-reader is a member of organization acme-demo but holds only a direct Read grant on acme-docs (her only team is frontend-child, which has no grant, and team hierarchy does not propagate), so the application's own predicate APP.canTriage(repo, carol-reader) is false, while bob-reviewer (direct Write) and the signed-in Owner are eligible. APP.assigneePicker, the picker actually used by the issue detail page, selects candidates by organization membership instead of repository permission, so it offers carol-reader as an assignable option.
subject: assigneePicker

explanation: REQ-6-3-3 requires that a draft started with Start a review stays pending — it is shown to its author with 'Pending review' but is not made public before review submission. The fixture uses the seeded public Open PR acme-docs#1 viewed by its author account alice-dev (an organization Owner, and a different account from the commenter bob-reviewer), and contains one already-published inline comment plus one unsubmitted (published:false) inline comment by bob-reviewer anchored to the same current compare commit c-acme-3. APP.pullFiles, the real Files-changed renderer, lists every inline record for the PR without any author or publication check, so bob-reviewer's unsubmitted draft body is rendered to alice-dev and is therefore public before submission.
subject: pullFiles
